goal: Build a fresh CS2 demo anomaly lab that autonomously discovers reviewed public samples online and proves a real parse-to-report run.
acceptance_criteria: A real input passes parser proof only when demoparser2 yields non-zero ticks and player states with positions and view angles; weapon_fire events are joined when present, and absent visibility or hearing telemetry remains unknown rather than inferred.

Acquisition is opt-in, bounded by requests, candidates, elapsed time, compressed and expanded bytes, and safe archive-member rules; authentication bypass, arbitrary-site crawling, traversal, symlinks, and unverified payloads are rejected.

Analysis labels yaw and pitch deltas as a view-angle movement proxy rather than raw mouse input and reports player relationships, angular error, snap-before-shot, tracking, switching, and information-timing evidence only where source coverage supports each signal.

Reports provide signal windows, coverage, confidence, provenance, limitations, and human-review guidance without automatic bans or definitive cheating accusations; unlabeled public demos cannot establish detection accuracy.

The CLI performs one real online discovery, download, extraction, parse, analysis, and JSON or HTML report run with synthetic fallback disabled, while unit and security tests prove candidate failover and acquisition boundaries.
The generated project passes its tests and runtime checks, and only local_packager creates the canonical delivery bundle through the existing delivery route.

The project dynamically enumerates multiple candidates from a reviewed public HTTPS catalog and records public visibility, repository license, immutable commit, object identity, expected size, expected SHA-256, and every candidate attempt.
The retired generated project, bundle, source cache, and runtime output are not reused; the replacement is created through the reviewed Provider generation route.

feedback: Fresh project autonomously discovered, verified, downloaded, parsed and analyzed a genuine public CS2 demo with truthful signal and information-coverage limits; formal Provider generation and canonical packaging remain incomplete.

worked: Real candidate failures drove source-format selection, path normalization, bounded analysis, evidence-fit Demo ranking and attributable shot provenance without weakening parser proof.
did_not_work: The reviewed Provider route hit the configured API usage limit and its registered local-model fallback repeatedly timed out on the backend manifest, so canonical production identity was never created.
experiments: Keep discovery cheap but rank extracted demos by goal-relevant event coverage before full parsing; retain large verified inputs outside the delivery tree and keep accuracy separate from pipeline execution.
